title: A fictional tidal-record archive
passage:
A
For much of the twentieth century, the port of Leston measured tides with a mechanical gauge housed in a small brick building. The instrument traced water height onto paper wrapped around a rotating drum. Each week an attendant replaced the paper and wrote the dates on its edge. Although the gauge operated at the harbour entrance, its records were later stored inland at the municipal library.

B
In 1984, a flood damaged part of the library basement. Archivists dried the surviving charts between sheets of absorbent material. They did not attempt to reconstruct the missing weeks: the remaining curves were continuous, but their dates alone could not establish the conditions on destroyed charts. A catalogue completed in 1992 identified gaps without estimating the heights that had been lost.

C
A later project sought to compare these historical measurements with modern digital readings. Before digitisation, technicians checked each chart's scale against notes made by the attendants. They found that the drum speed had changed twice, so a fixed conversion from horizontal distance to time would have produced misleading comparisons. The team therefore used the dated notes to select the appropriate time scale for each chart.

D
The project's director, Mara Venn, argued that the greatest value of the archive lay not in any single exceptional tide but in repeated observations made at one location. She cautioned, however, that the port's later construction work altered local water movement. In her view, a comparison that ignored those changes would exaggerate what the old measurements could reveal about regional trends. The team published the digitised curves together with a list of known gaps and changes in methods.

E
Teachers subsequently used excerpts from the archive in classroom exercises. Students compared the shape of selected curves, then discussed why an incomplete record should not be treated as a complete history. The library also displayed the mechanical drum, although the display did not state how much it had originally cost.
